findings_addressed.oracle: provider.is_connected is asserted False after the production connect() path receives a deterministic 401 HTTP response. The 401 is injected via httpx.MockTransport at the external transport boundary (the outbound HTTP socket); connect() production code runs fully unmodified. The exception branch (except httpx.HTTPStatusError, openrouter.py ~line 186) is always entered, so the assertion is unconditional — not conditioned on live API behaviour.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In openrouter.py ~line 186, change `self.connected = False` to `self.connected = True` inside the `except httpx.HTTPStatusError` branch. With that mutation, connect() sets connected=True before raising AuthenticationError, causing `assert provider.is_connected is False` to fail with AssertionError. The test is unconditionally falsifiable because the mock transport guarantees a 401 is always returned.

notes: Previous version used an if/else branch accepting both 'AuthenticationError raised' and 'connect succeeds' as valid outcomes (N7 accepts-both-outcomes). The re-hardened test eliminates the disjunction by injecting a deterministic 401 response via httpx.MockTransport so the except httpx.HTTPStatusError branch is always entered. pytest.raises(AuthenticationError) asserts the exception is always raised; the follow-up assertion asserts is_connected is always False. A mutation setting connected=True in the except branch reliably breaks the assertion.
